newsitem.title: USA: U.S. quiet in dispute with India over diplomats.
newsitem.headline: U.S. quiet in dispute with India over diplomats.

text.p: The U.S. State Department and the Central Intelligence Agency had no immediate comment on Thursday on a flap with India involving two U.S. diplomats but officials said the issue was being discussed with New Delhi.
One official told Reuters the two diplomats, who have not been identified, had not left India and he suggested the dispute had more to do with Indian domestic politics than substance.
The Hindustan Times reported on Thursday that India will ask two U.S. diplomats to leave after an Indian intelligence official was accused of having unauthorised links with them.
The newspaper did not name the diplomats but said one was the local CIA station director.
In Washignton the CIA declined comment. The State Department was said to be drafting a statement.
It was unclear if the Foreign Ministry told U.S. Ambassador Frank Wisner of the decision because Indian Foreign Secretary Salman Haider was on leave, the Hindustan Times said.
"We see this as an internal Indian government matter," a U.S. embassy spokeswoman in New Delhi said. She declined to elaborate.
"It is not the policy of the government to comment on such media reports," an Indian Foreign Ministry spokesman said.

The Hindustan Times said the decision to ask "the Americans to leave quietly" was made at a meeting of senior civil servants, including the chief of the home (interior) and foreign intelligence departments, and senior Home Ministry officials.
